chunks: Samāʿah asked him about a slave whose master enters into a mukātabah contract with him while knowing that he possesses neither a little nor much wealth. He said:

Let him enter into the mukātabah with him, even if he has to ask people. His lacking wealth should not prevent the mukātabah, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, provides the servants through one another, so the doer of good is aided.

key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave who is the subject of the emancipation contract
key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبَةُ: the contract of emancipation by agreed payment
key_terms.يُكَاتِبُهُ: he contracts with him for manumission through mukatabah

ai.seo_question: Can a poor slave with no wealth still be given a mukataba contract?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the contract of manumission, stating that a master's knowledge of the slave's poverty does not prevent making a mukātabah contract. It also highlights reliance upon Allah's provision through people and encourages facilitating good and emancipation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3481 - Sama'ah asked him about a slave whose master enters into a mukataba (a contract of emancipation) with him, knowing that the slave possesses neither a little nor much wealth.

Imam (as) said: "Let him enter into the mukataba, even if the slave has to ask others for help. The lack of wealth should not prevent the contract, for Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, provides sustenance to His servants through one another. The one who does good is supported."
